parts:
Hello Dr. Broman,

As part of an undergraduate research project, I have successfully been able to produce a high quality genetic map for a species of interest. In order to continue my analysis, I need to add an additional ~700 markers that were not included in the production of the original map. These were not used initially because they are relatively noisy i.e. the genotypes are not as high quality for technical reasons, but they are really interesting. I do not wish to start a new map from scratch using both the high and low quality markers but rather somehow add the new markers into a final map that was produced using only the high quality markers.

My issue begins with the fact that the new markers are not present in the original input file that I used to make the final map, and I am unsure of how to add this data while maintaining the final order of the original markers. Do you have any recommendations on how to approach this in an efficient manner?

I would really appreciate any advice.

Thank you for your time.

Best,
Lucydalila

messages.subject: Adding new markers to a completed genetic mapa completed genetic map
parts:
I would create a file with all of the markers, read it into R, and then use movemarker() to move markers to the linkage groups and locations you'd previously identified.

karl
